## Context / Problem
Found 2026-11-23 PST by the LLM-Review of Gerrit change 3535 (immoral-heated-doctorfish follow-up). `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh` deletes the review-bot's `default` Gerrit token and then has Gerrit generate a new one before it stores the token in SSM. Since 35c1983cb07 it prints a notice when the generator output has the wrong shape: Gerrit's token was already replaced, SSM was not updated, and the review-bot cannot authenticate until a re-run succeeds. 2 other failures after the delete leave the bot in the same broken state with no such notice, because `set -euo pipefail` exits silently on them:
- `gerrit set-account --generate-http-password` exits non-zero.
- `aws ssm put-parameter` fails (expired AWS session, missing permission).

An operator rotating the token would then see a bare non-zero exit and might not know the bot is now locked out.

## Root cause
Reproduced 2026-11-23 PST against a copy of the script with PATH stubs: a failing generator (exit 1), a failing `aws` (exit 254), and a SIGTERM during the `aws` call each end the script (rc 1, 254, 143) with no notice. The notice lives only in the one explicit shape-check branch; every other way out between the delete and the SSM write is an implicit `set -e` exit or a signal, which runs no code.

## Approach
Fix the class rather than add more per-step branches. Just before the `--delete-token default` call (the point of no return) arm an `EXIT` trap that prints the notice ("Gerrit's token for '<bot>' was already replaced and SSM was NOT updated; the review-bot cannot authenticate until this script succeeds") to stderr, plus `INT`/`TERM`/`HUP` traps that `exit 130/143/129` so a signal also exits non-zero and runs the `EXIT` trap. Disarm all four (`trap - EXIT INT TERM HUP`) immediately after `aws ssm put-parameter` succeeds, before step 5 installs its own cleanup trap. The shape-check branch keeps its "unexpected --generate-http-password output (value not printed)" line and its `exit 1`, and relies on the trap for the notice instead of duplicating it. The notice prints only `$BOT_USER`, never `$TOKEN` or the generator output. No new config key, environment variable, or flag.

## Scope
- `infra/gerrit/service-user.sh`: arm/disarm the traps around step 3-4; remove the duplicated notice lines from the shape-check branch.
- `tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py`: let the existing argv-recording `ssh` and `aws` stubs fail on demand, and add the failure-path test.

## Testing
New parametrized test in `tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py`, through the existing argv-recording stubs, one case per failure point after the delete:
- generator prints `New password: <token>` and then exits 1;
- `aws ssm put-parameter` reads the token from stdin and exits 254 with an error on stderr;
- `aws` sends SIGTERM to the script mid-write (interrupted operator run).
Each case asserts a non-zero exit, the "already replaced" / "SSM was NOT" / "cannot authenticate" notice on stderr, and that the token appears in neither stdout, stderr nor the recorded argv. Each case is run against the unfixed script first to confirm it fails there. The existing happy-path test asserts the notice is absent on success, and the existing shape-check tests keep passing unchanged. `make verify` runs the whole suite, including the doctorfish argv guard, before push.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When `service-user.sh` fails at any step after deleting the bot's `default` token and before the SSM write succeeds, it tells the operator on stderr that Gerrit's token was replaced, SSM was not updated, and the review-bot cannot authenticate until the script succeeds, without printing the token.
- [ ] A test drives the generator-failure and SSM-failure paths through the existing argv-recording stubs (`tests/scripts/test_operator_credential_argv.py`) and asserts the notice, a non-zero exit, and that the token appears in no output or argv.
